subject: Film & Cinema
title: High Fantasy on Film
description: A 60-second lesson on High Fantasy on Film.

hook.text: For decades, everyone said Lord of the Rings was unfilmable. Peter Jackson disagreed.

buildup.text: High fantasy requires world-building — languages, histories, and maps audiences believe in.

discovery.text: Jackson's trilogy proved CGI and practical effects could bring imagined worlds to life.

twist.text: Most fantasy films that followed copied the template without matching the craft.

climax.text: High fantasy works on screen only when the emotional stakes match the visual scale.

punchline.text: The ring was small. The story was enormous.

quiz.question: What did Peter Jackson prove with Lord of the Rings?
options: Massive fantasy worlds can work on screen with the right craft
